findings.claim: ac553PlannedFiles reaches into the CLI's module-level `filePath` const declared 529 lines below it
findings.analysis: scripts/task-graph.mjs line 189 evaluates `typeof filePath === 'string' ? path.dirname(filePath) : process.cwd()` inside a helper defined at line 180, while `const filePath` is declared at module top level at line 718. This works today because every call happens from command handlers that execute after line 718, but `typeof` on a lexically-declared module binding is a temporal-dead-zone ReferenceError if the helper is ever invoked during module evaluation, and the implicit coupling makes the helper silently cwd-fallback if the file is ever split into a library. Functional at HEAD; fragile style only.
findings.proposed_fix: Thread the graph file path into ac553PlannedFiles/ac553EffectiveFlags/assertDesignTechRiskGate as an explicit parameter (validate-task-graph-lane.mjs already does exactly this at its line 211).

findings.claim: Explicit --subject/--body override narrows the named-WI merge gate to caller-supplied text
findings.analysis: In scripts/merge-pr-with-review-receipt.mjs collectPrProvenance (lines 131-142), when the caller passes --subject/--body/--net-files, the gate evaluates ONLY that explicit text and skips fetching the PR's real title/body/commits. A caller can merge a PR whose GitHub body names WIs by passing a WI-free --subject. Mitigating: with --squash the explicit subject/body IS the landed commit message, so the durable record matches exactly what was checked, and the gh-fetched default path (the one land-changeset/worktree.sh use) is fully gated. Residual risk is limited to deliberate operator override.
findings.proposed_fix: When --subject/--body are explicit AND a PR number resolves, additionally fetch the PR body and union its named WIs into namedWis (net files still from --net-files or the PR file list).

findings.claim: Named-WI net-diff evidence uses substring matching, so a longer WI id can satisfy a shorter one
findings.analysis: missingNamedWis (scripts/merge-pr-with-review-receipt.mjs lines 27-38) tests `file.includes(token)` with token 'wi-553'; a net file named for WI-5533 (e.g. docs/specs/work-items/WI-5533.md) contains 'wi-553' as a substring and would count as evidence for WI-553. Requires an adjacent WI id that shares a prefix, so practical exposure is small.
findings.proposed_fix: Match the token with a trailing non-digit boundary, e.g. new RegExp(`${token}(?![0-9])`).
